title: AEE Deep Focus State
description: Where focus is, as the focus observer records it: DOM focus followed through shadow roots and frames, where the accessibility tree has focus, and whether the interaction's target has it.

requestedTarget.description: Whether the element the interaction's target names, found in the page by Playwright as the action found it (page.locator for a selector, page.getByRole for a role and name), is the element with focus. focused: the target matches one element and that element has focus; not-focused: it matches one element and focus is on another, or deeper inside it; unresolved: which element it means, or whether that one has focus, cannot be told (reason). Recorded when the interaction's target has a selector, or a role and a name.

exact.description: Whether name is the whole accessible name (true, the default) or a part of it, as getByRole takes it.

domFocusState.description: Where DOM focus is, followed through shadow roots and frames: the element with focus, with the active element of each document on the way to it.

documentHasFocus.description: The top document's hasFocus(): whether focus is in the page at all. When no element of a document has focus, its <body> is its active element, both when focus is lost inside the page (true) and when Tab has moved focus out of the page to the browser's own controls (false).

deepActiveElement.description: The element that has focus, in whichever shadow root or frame holds it.

activeElementChain.description: Each active element from the top document's down to the one with focus.

element.description: How an element with focus, or on the way to it, looks and where it sits; its role, name, states, dialog and composite widget are the accessibility tree's, which is what NVDA and JAWS receive from Chrome. They are absent when the tree does not have the element.

type.description: A form control's type, such as checkbox.

compositeItemIndex.description: Its place among the widget's items, counted from 0, in the order the tree has them.

nodePath.description: Its path in the document that holds it, as axe-core writes it in a result's target: the shortest selector that selects it alone, with each step into a shadow root after ">>>".

frameId.description: The frame whose document holds the element.

framePath.description: The <iframe> elements the element is inside, outermost first, each as its nodePath in the document that holds it. Absent in the top document.

backendDOMNodeId.description: The DOM node, as the browser session numbers it in its frame's process; recorded for the element with focus in each document. With frameId it joins the element to accessibilityFocus and to the frame's accessibility tree.

focusOrderIndex.description: The element's place in the page's tab order, counted from 0 across the top document and every frame: each document's tab stops as tabbable orders them, and each frame's tab stops at its <iframe> element's place, as Chrome's Tab moves through them. Places compare across frames. Absent when the element is not a tab stop (focusableCount is then still recorded), or when a frame's place or tab stops could not be read (and focusableCount is absent too).

focusableCount.description: How many tab stops the page has, across the top document and every frame. Recorded whenever the page's tab order was counted, so an element with focusableCount and no focusOrderIndex is known not to be a tab stop: a document's <body> without a place is then no element having focus, not a frame's own tab stop.
